partial:
partial Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\bar\chi(g) = O(\mathrm{LR}(g))\)
    BBGM22
    Immediate from the optimality of $\mathrm{LR}$: any measure satisfying the inner composition theorem is $O(\mathrm{LR})$.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\exists \text{ partial } g:\ \mathrm{LR}(g) = \bar\chi(g)^{1+\Omega(1)}\)
    BBGM22
    A polynomial separation; this is what makes $\mathrm{LR}$ a strictly better inner measure.
see also: \(\mathrm{LR}(f)\), \(\bar{\chi}(f)\), comp-R data/relations/04-composition.yaml

facts: $\mathrm{LR}$ can be polynomially larger than $\bar{\chi}$ [BBGM22].
Total functions have $\mathrm{R}/\mathrm{LR}=\Omega(\log N)$ and $\mathrm{LR}/\bar\chi=\Omega(\sqrt{\log N})$ [Meiburg26composition]; see \(M_q\) and \(G_q\).
self.name: Linearised randomized complexity
self.short: The largest measure satisfying an inner composition theorem R(f o g) = Omega(R(f) LR(g)).

up.note: Linearised randomized complexity lower-bounds the asymptotic composition rate. Whether it equals it is the open problem posed in that paper.

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
